item.text:
**Bottom line**
Putin’s 2024 record on `3B.7` is mostly negative. There is some real, but limited, evidence of family benefits and emergency shelter for evacuees, yet the stronger pattern is the opposite: child-transfer allegations, coercive treatment of vulnerable minorities/migrants, and continued civilian harm in occupied areas.

**Evidence For**

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Government meeting on support for large families](https://government.ru/en/news/50700/) | Government of Russia | 2024-01-25 | https://government.ru/en/news/50700/ | The government said the president had signed an order making equal support for families with three or more children available nationwide, regardless of region. This is broad family support, not violence protection, but it is a concrete pro-family measure for a vulnerable group. | `3B.7` |
| [Government expanded support for citizens caring for disabled people](https://government.ru/news/50822/) | Government of Russia | 2024-02-08 | https://government.ru/news/50822/ | From 2024, parents and guardians caring for disabled children could keep the monthly allowance even if they worked part-time, including remotely. This is a direct support measure for a vulnerable group, though not a security-protection reform. | `3B.7` |
| [Our Regions: Social Fund Operations in Donbas, Zaporozhye, and Kherson Regions in 2024](https://sfr.gov.ru/en/press_center/~2024/12/18/276536) | Social Fund of Russia | 2024-12-18 | https://sfr.gov.ru/en/press_center/~2024/12/18/276536 | The Social Fund reported full-scale service coverage in occupied/new regions, including child benefits, payments for pregnant women, disability support, and health-worker payments. This shows administrative support for vulnerable civilians, but it sits inside a war/occupation framework. | `3B.7`, also `2B.10` |
| [Children evacuated from Kursk region stay at a temporary accommodation centre in Moscow region](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/children-evacuated-from-kursk-region-stay-at-a-temporary-accommodation-centre-in-moscow-region/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjQ6bmV3c21sX1JDMjlROUFLNjQwVA) | Reuters Connect | 2024-08-30 | https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/children-evacuated-from-kursk-region-stay-at-a-temporary-accommodation-centre-in-moscow-region/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjQ6bmV3c21sX1JDMjlROUFLNjQwVA | Reuters’ caption shows children, including from orphanages, evacuated from the Kursk region being housed in temporary accommodation. This is a concrete protective response for displaced children, but it is reactive wartime shelter rather than evidence of durable protection. | `3B.7`, also `3B.6` |

**Evidence Against**

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Putin's Kremlin planes took away Ukrainian children for adoption, report alleges](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/exclusiveputincontrolled-aircraft-deported-ukrainian-children-usbacked-research-alleges-3750835) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-12-03 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/exclusiveputincontrolled-aircraft-deported-ukrainian-children-usbacked-research-alleges-3750835 | Yale-backed research alleged Russian state aircraft and funds were used in a Kremlin-directed program that removed children from occupied Ukrainian territory, stripped identity, and placed them with Russian families. It is an allegation, not a judicial finding, but if accurate it is strong evidence against protecting children and against preventing forced displacement. | `3B.7`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2` |
| [Russia 'Punishes' Tajik Migrants With Entry Denials, Deportations After Terror Attack](https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-punishes-tajik-migrants-deportations-entry-moscow-terror-attack/32891458.html) | RFE/RL | 2024-04-04 | https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-punishes-tajik-migrants-deportations-entry-moscow-terror-attack/32891458.html | After Crocus, police raids, entry denials, deportations, and aggressive questioning targeted Tajik migrants. That looks like collective punishment and intimidation of a vulnerable ethnic/migrant group, not protection. | `3B.7`, also `3B.2`, `3B.6` |
| [Ukraine human rights situation remains bleak three years after Russia’s full-scale armed attack](https://ukraine.un.org/en/286771-ukraine-human-rights-situation-remains-bleak-three-years-after-russia%E2%80%99s-full-scale-armed) | United Nations in Ukraine | 2024-12-31 | https://ukraine.un.org/en/286771-ukraine-human-rights-situation-remains-bleak-three-years-after-russia%E2%80%99s-full-scale-armed | The UN said civilian casualties were rising, executions and torture of POWs continued, and control was being entrenched in occupied territory. This is strong evidence that Putin’s war posture did not protect civilians, displaced people, or other vulnerable groups from systematic harm. | `3B.7`, also `3B.1`, `2B.10` |

**Search gap**
I found limited positive evidence for vulnerable groups, but it is mostly general welfare policy or reactive evacuation/shelter. I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Putin established durable protections against targeted violence, forced displacement, or systematic neglect for women, children, minorities, or other vulnerable groups, especially in occupied territory.
